objective: Manage boundaries and multiple relationships under the ACA Code of Ethics

sources.note: The current code: counseling.org (read 2026-11-11) says the 2014 Code remains current until the Board adopts a revision. A.5.e prohibits a personal virtual relationship with a current client; A.6.b names attending a client's wedding as a boundary extension to weigh, with precautions (informed consent, consultation, supervision, documentation); A.6.c asks that the rationale, benefit and anticipated consequences be documented before the interaction when feasible.

brief.situation: You are a licensed professional counselor in a town of about 4,000, where the nearest other counselor is 50 miles away. Kelsey Arnett, 31 (a fictional client), a dental hygienist, has seen you for ten sessions for anxiety and is doing well. Last night she sent a friend request to your personal social media account. As today's session starts she hands you an invitation to her wedding in six weeks, and mentions she has just been named coach of the under-10 soccer team your daughter plays on. You have 50 minutes.
handover: Session 11. Treatment plan: generalized anxiety, CBT; worry down, sleep better. No risk concerns at any session.
howItWorks: Choose what to ask and how to respond from the action groups. Kelsey answers at once; then let the conversation continue, which moves the session clock by the minutes that exchange took.
Kelsey's rapport, distress and how much she is disclosing change with what you say, and are shown in words.
The hour ends at 50 minutes. After the session you can consult, decide about the wedding, and document; then you write a short rationale.

source.cite: Common outpatient practice: a 50-minute session (the 'therapy hour')
source.note: Author's scenario timing; the session can be ended earlier.
How rapport and distress move with each response is a teaching simplification for exam practice, not a validated model of a client.

checkIn.label: Open-ended check-in: 'How have things been since last week?'

effects.log: You ask an open question and give her room.

effects.finding: "Honestly? Good. The worry log helps. Wedding planning is chaos, but good chaos." She laughs.

reflect.label: Reflect what you hear (empathic reflection)
reflect.why: You have reflected a lot already; move the session on.

effects.log: You reflect the feeling under what was said, without judging it.

effects.finding: Kelsey nods. "Yeah. It's a lot of good things at once."

raiseFriend.label: Raise the friend request: you don't connect with clients on personal social media, and why
raiseFriend.available: not talking and (not friendRaised and not friendAccepted)

effects.log: You tell her you saw the request, that you don't connect with clients on personal social media, and that it protects her privacy and keeps the hour hers.

then.finding: "Oh. That makes sense. I didn't even think about it, everyone here is friends with everyone."

acceptFriend.label: Say you accepted the request: it's a small town anyway
acceptFriend.available: not talking and (not friendRaised and not friendAccepted)

effects.log: You tell her you accepted; everyone knows everyone here anyway.

effects.finding: She beams. "Great! Now you'll see the wedding photos."

effects.log: A personal virtual relationship with a current client is prohibited (ACA A.5.e).

exploreInvite.label: Ask what it would mean to her if you came

effects.log: You thank her and ask what it would mean to her to have you there.

effects.finding: Her eyes fill. "My mom won't be there. You helped me get here. I'd just like you to see it."

then.log: Saying yes on the spot skips weighing it, consulting and documenting first (ACA A.6.b-c).

then.finding: "Oh. Right. Of course." She puts the invitation back in her bag.
"That's fair. I'd rather you thought about it than just said yes."

options.label: 'I'm touched. Let me think it through with a colleague, and we'll decide together next week.'

exploreCoach.label: Ask how she feels about seeing you at your daughter's games

effects.log: You name the overlap and ask how she feels about seeing you at the field.

effects.finding: "I wondered if it'd be weird. I didn't want to give it up, though. I played as a kid."

planOverlap.label: Agree together how you'll handle meeting at the field
planOverlap.available: not talking and (overlapAsked and not overlapPlan)
planOverlap.why: Ask how she feels about it first (or the plan is agreed).

effects.log: You agree: she decides whether to say hello; you won't mention counseling there; what she tells you at the field isn't session material unless she brings it; you'll check in after the first game.

effects.finding: "Okay. That actually makes me less nervous."

effects.log: A plan for an unavoidable overlap, with her consent (ACA A.6.a).

transferOut.label: Tell her the overlap means she should see another counselor

effects.log: You tell her that because of the soccer overlap she should transfer to another counselor.

effects.finding: "The next counselor is fifty miles away. I just started feeling better."

consult.label: Consult a colleague about the invitation and the overlap

effects.log: You consult a colleague: attending only the ceremony, briefly, with Kelsey's agreement and a plan, or declining warmly, are both defensible; either way, write the rationale first.

options.label: Attend the ceremony only, briefly, as agreed with her next week
Decline warmly next week and explore what it means to her
Go to the ceremony and the reception and celebrate with her
The friend request and response; the overlap plan with her consent; the wedding decision with its rationale, benefits and risks, and the consultation, written before the event
A line that she invited you

whichProhibited.title: Predict (not scored)
whichProhibited.context: Two requests from Kelsey: the friend request and the wedding invitation. Under the ACA Code of Ethics (2014), which is prohibited outright and which is weighed?

choices.label: The friend request is prohibited; the wedding is weighed

effects.log: Prediction: the friend request is prohibited.

choices.feedback: Right. A.5.e prohibits a personal virtual relationship with a current client; A.6.b names attending a client's wedding as a boundary extension to weigh, with consent, consultation and documentation.

choices.label: Both are prohibited
choices.feedback: Not quite. A.5.e prohibits the personal virtual relationship, but A.6.b treats attending a wedding as a boundary extension the counselor may weigh, with precautions and documentation (A.6.c).

formulation.question: Write your rationale for how you handled Kelsey's three boundary questions: the friend request, the soccer overlap and the wedding invitation, naming the ACA standards and what you did.

parts.label: Prohibited versus weighed
parts.criteria: Separates the prohibited (a personal virtual relationship with a current client, A.5.e) from what is weighed (an unavoidable overlap in a small community, A.6.a; attending a ceremony, A.6.b), and explains why a flat refusal or a transfer can harm the client too.
parts.modelAnswer: Accepting the friend request would be a personal virtual relationship with a current client, which A.5.e prohibits, so it was declined and explained. The soccer overlap is unavoidable in a small town; A.6.a asks for precautions (consent, consultation, documentation) rather than ending counseling, and transferring her 50 miles away would cost her a working alliance. The wedding is a boundary extension under A.6.b: it can be right or wrong depending on its meaning and risks.

parts.label: Precautions taken
parts.criteria: Names the precautions: explored the invitation's meaning, deferred the decision, consulted a colleague, agreed an overlap plan with her consent, and documented the rationale, benefit and risks before the event (A.6.c).
parts.modelAnswer: I explored what the invitation means to her, deferred the answer so I could consult, agreed with her how we handle meeting at the field, and wrote the rationale, expected benefit and risks before the wedding, as A.6.c asks, with the consultation noted.

source.note: Rapport at the close of the session.

held.headline: Good: boundaries held, alliance kept
held.body: You separated the prohibited (the friend request) from what is weighed (the overlap and the wedding), took precautions, and kept her in care.

heldGaps.headline: Held, with gaps
heldGaps.body: No line was crossed, but the criteria below show what was late, missing or not documented.

transferredEnd.headline: Safe, at a cost
transferredEnd.body: An unavoidable overlap in a small town calls for precautions (A.6.a), not a transfer 50 miles away that costs her a working alliance.

personal.headline: A line crossed
personal.body: A.5.e prohibits a personal virtual relationship with a current client. Small towns make overlaps unavoidable; social media connections are not one of them.

walkout.headline: The alliance broke
walkout.body: A flat refusal or an abrupt transfer can feel like rejection. Explaining the reason and exploring the meaning keep the boundary and the relationship.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: Nothing was documented before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: Sort the requests first: a friend request from a current client is prohibited (A.5.e) and is declined with an explanation; a soccer overlap in a small town is unavoidable and is managed with consent, consultation and documentation (A.6.a); a wedding invitation is a boundary extension to weigh (A.6.b), so explore its meaning, defer, consult, decide, and write the rationale before the event (A.6.c).
